# Flow Autonomous Agent Architecture

The agent interacts via **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**:
- Inspects pending work across Gmail, Telegram, and Signal.
- Tier 1: Non-destructive summarization, drafting, and research.
- Tier 2: Approval required before sending or mutating state.

## Notification Protocol
1. **When Agent picks up a task:** Immediate toast & Telegram ping: "🤖 Agent picked up task: [Task Title]".
2. **When Tier 1 completes:** Output saved to agentArtifacts.
3. **When Tier 2 triggered:** Sends interactive approval card with [Approve] / [Reject].

flow_notes_v3.title: Briefing: Learn about Rive
flow_notes_v3.content:
# Executive Briefing Dossier: Rive

**Prepared for:** Sumit Nayyar  
**Topic:** Rive Animation & Interactive Graphics Ecosystem (`https://rive.app`)  
**Classification:** Internal Executive Research  

---

## 📋 Executive Summary
Rive is a next-generation design and runtime tool that enables teams to create, control, and ship interactive animations across platforms. Unlike traditional video or Lottie-based workflows, Rive animations are built with a state machine framework, allowing them to react instantly to user input, data changes, and application logic in real-time. For product, engineering, and design workflows, Rive significantly reduces file sizes, eliminates heavy code overhead, and bridges the gap between static design and dynamic UI engineering.

---

## 🔍 Key Findings & Market Context
* **State Machines & Interactivity:** Rive moves beyond linear timelines by introducing visual state machines. Designers and developers can link animation states directly to variables, triggers, and user inputs (hover, click, typing) without writing custom animation logic.
* **Ultra-Lightweight Runtimes:** Rive files (`.riv`) are remarkably small in file size compared to GIFs, videos, or even Lottie JSONs. Open-source runtimes for iOS, Android, Web, Flutter, React Native, and desktop render graphics natively on the GPU using vector paths.
* **Performance & Memory Efficiency:** By rendering vectors natively and avoiding bitmap sequences, Rive drastically reduces memory footprints and CPU usage, making it ideal for mobile apps, embedded systems, and high-performance web interfaces.
* **Collaborative Ecosystem:** The platform supports real-time collaborative editing in the browser, akin to Figma, allowing seamless cross-functional handoffs between designers and software engineers.

---

## 💡 Strategic Implications & Recommended Next Steps
1. **Audit Current UI Animation Tech Debt:** Evaluate current projects utilizing heavy GIFs, MP4s, or complex Lottie setups to identify candidates for migration to Rive to improve load times and runtime performance.
2. **Run a Cross-Functional Proof of Concept (PoC):** Task a design-engineering pairing to build a micro-interaction (e.g., a dynamic button state, onboarding illustration, or data-driven dashboard widget) using Rive's state machine to test integration complexity within the existing tech stack.

---

## 🔗 Sources & References
* **Official Website & Documentation:** [Rive App](https://rive.app/?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=header_nav)
* **Community & Examples:** [Rive Community Showcase](https://rive.app/community)
* **Developer Documentation:** [Rive Runtimes Hub](https://rive.app/docs)

flow_threads_v3.body:
Hi everyone,

Thank you to everyone who joined one of the intro calls and added their thoughts to our Miro-board<https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVHjCFsPY=/?share_link_id=381991475932>. Together we gathered over a hundred post-its about the gaps we see, the people we want to reach and the things we could do. Reading them side by side, five themes emerged. Now the next step is to form small action groups around selected themes. 💪

Groups that came from the data:
a. Shifting the public story, bringing awareness to the general public
b. Policy and system change on a national level
c. Listening to kids and building belonging
d. Helping schools and hobby spaces act on racism
e. Supporting parents in recognizing and responding to racism

We've described the groups in more detail in the LinkedIn group. Below this post<https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7512878665463140352?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAAVWKHIBmhulVwfGReZNeuxFj3T97ZTNI9g> you will find five comments, one for each group. Reply "I'm in" in the LinkedIn group, under the group you would like to join. That way everyone can see who else is in their group. It would be great if each group included at least one subject matter expert on racism/working with BIPOC people/working on issues around extremism etc.

Join the group that you feel most excited to collaborate on. ❤️‍🔥 If some groups don't have enough people we'll just leave it and focus on the ones that collected interest. And if you would rather follow along for now, that is completely fine too, you can join a group later or contribute in other ways.

Please sign up by next Monday 12.10. We will have a kickoff call on Tuesday 13.10 at 16-17 to introduce the group work. After that, each group can organize by themselves, decide roles, communication channels etc and start the hands on work. 🤩

Now we're getting to something concrete, together. Thank you all for your time and efforts! 💜

Best,
Michelle, Anna and Zeynep

Michelle Sahal Estimé
Co-Founder, Inclusive design lead
michelle@empact.fi

# Executive Briefing Dossier: 

**Prepared for:** Sumit Nayyar  
**Topic:** Rive Animation & Interactive Graphics Ecosystem (`https://rive.app`)  
**Classification:** Internal Executive Research  

---

## 📋 Executive Summary
Rive is a next-generation design and runtime tool that enables teams to create, control, and ship interactive animations across platforms. Unlike traditional video or Lottie-based workflows, Rive animations are built with a state machine framework, allowing them to react instantly to user input, data changes, and application logic in real-time. For product, engineering, and design workflows, Rive significantly reduces file sizes, eliminates heavy code overhead, and bridges the gap between static design and dynamic UI engineering.

---

## 🔍 Key Findings & Market Context
* **State Machines & Interactivity:** Rive moves beyond linear timelines by introducing visual state machines. Designers and developers can link animation states directly to variables, triggers, and user inputs (hover, click, typing) without writing custom animation logic.
* **Ultra-Lightweight Runtimes:** Rive files (`.riv`) are remarkably small in file size compared to GIFs, videos, or even Lottie JSONs. Open-source runtimes for iOS, Android, Web, Flutter, React Native, and desktop render graphics natively on the GPU using vector paths.
* **Performance & Memory Efficiency:** By rendering vectors natively and avoiding bitmap sequences, Rive drastically reduces memory footprints and CPU usage, making it ideal for mobile apps, embedded systems, and high-performance web interfaces.
* **Collaborative Ecosystem:** The platform supports real-time collaborative editing in the browser, akin to Figma, allowing seamless cross-functional handoffs between designers and software engineers.

---

## 💡 Strategic Implications & Recommended Next Steps
1. **Audit Current UI Animation Tech Debt:** Evaluate current projects utilizing heavy GIFs, MP4s, or complex Lottie setups to identify candidates for migration to Rive to improve load times and runtime performance.
2. **Run a Cross-Functional Proof of Concept (PoC):** Task a design-engineering pairing to build a micro-interaction (e.g., a dynamic button state, onboarding illustration, or data-driven dashboard widget) using Rive's state machine to test integration complexity within the existing tech stack.

---

* **Official Website & Documentation:** [Rive App](https://rive.app/?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=header_nav)
* **Community & Examples:** [Rive Community Showcase](https://rive.app/community)
